item.title: China brands drop Mbappe for ‘offending national sentiments’
item.description: Kylian Mbappe was dropped on Tuesday by major Chinese brands after a video circulated of the Real Madrid and France superstar apparently joking about Mao Zedong. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sports drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media. Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line”. Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. Asked on Tuesday about the controversy, China’s foreign ministry said that it was aware of the reports. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and that all advertisements involving Mbappe have also been removed. item.title: Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award
item.description: Barcelona and Spain forward Vicky López has paid an emotional tribute to her late Nigerian mother, Joy Felix, after winning the Women’s Young Player of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday. The 20-year-old attacking midfielder dedicated the honour to her mother, who died when she was 11, saying she continued to feel her presence despite her absence. “Mum, although you can’t be with me physically, I feel your presence every day. Everything I’ve achieved I owe to you, so thank you for teaching me never to give up,” López said. “Thank you to everyone in football and let’s keep making this sport better.” The Barcelona star, whose father is Spanish and mother Nigerian, was born in 2006 in Vallecas, a working-class neighbourhood in Madrid. Her journey in football began at an early age, playing in the streets with her older brother, Jesus, when she was just four. Spanish football journalist Irati Vidal told BBC Sport that López’s style was heavily influenced by street football, where she developed the flair, agility and speed that have become part of her game. “Vicky learned her craft on the streets of Vallecas, her style is very street-influenced,” Vidal said. “She used to play for fun while admiring and trying to copy Neymar’s dribbles.” López’s latest recognition follows an impressive 2025-26 campaign in which Barcelona won Liga F, the Copa de la Reina, the Supercopa de España and the UEFA Women’s Champions League. The award was her second consecutive Women’s Young Player of the Year honour, having also won the inaugural edition in 2025. Beyond her club achievements, López has set her sights on representing Spain at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. “I think wearing the Spain shirt is a dream that all girls who play football have,” she told Antena 3 Deportes. “For me, winning a World Cup with Spain would be one of the greatest achievements.” Her ambition is also tied to the memory of her mother, whom she has described as a major source of motivation. “For me, my mother is everything. A goal I have in life is to make her proud.” The post Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [NESG] We’re rewriting Nigeria’s story of underperformance – Tinubu
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu saying at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) in Abuja that his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. Another headline features the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, saying Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases following the medical evacuation of the patient and her husband to Switzerland. Vanguard also reports that an investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian reports that despite 25 State Houses of Assembly endorsing the State Police Bill, persistent fears over political interference, human rights violations and weak accountability have raised questions about whether the proposed safeguards can protect citizens from abuse or remain largely theoretical. The Punch leads with organised labour looking forward to its next action after a crucial meeting with the Federal Government on Tuesday, with the Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress demanding concrete proposals on petrol prices, wage negotiations and other unresolved workers’ welfare issues amid the threat of nationwide industrial action. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said some Nigerians spend as much as 120 per cent of their income on food, forcing them to borrow money or rely on relatives to survive. item.title: Houthi official says Egypt’s military support for Saudi declaration of war
item.description: A Houthi official said Tuesday that the Egyptian parliament’s decision to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia to defend against the Iran-backed group’s attacks was a declaration of war. The comment was part of a long statement reacting to a Monday visit to Tehran by the Saudi defence minister, alongside Pakistan’s army chief and Turkey’s intelligence chief, in a bid to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East war. “It is truly remarkable that while these people go to discuss what they call ‘peace in the region’, Egypt and its parliament declare support for the so-called defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, declare war against the Republic of Yemen,” said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, in a Telegram post. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief General Asim Munir and Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin attended the talks with Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. They also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Iran, Pakistan and Turkey recently signed a Nato-style defence pact in Mecca that says an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three. But since the Houthis ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia earlier this month, the two other countries have not announced any strikes on the group. Al-Houthi said the pact was “a clear and blatant act of aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran”, adding that the group was “not afraid of any alliance that may be formed”. In July, Yemen’s conflict flared up again as a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa, in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks. The Houthis then declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast. In response, the Houthis have reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control. In October, the Houthis ramped up their attacks on Saudi Arabia, forcing the cancellation of flagship events and a shutdown of Riyadh airport for two weeks. item.title: DSS arraigns man over fake Tinubu letter to US president
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against a Kaduna man accused of circulating a fake letter purportedly written by President Bola Tinubu to the President of the United States. The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi, also known as Sardaunan Samari, was arrested on September 28 after allegedly sharing the document on his Facebook page with the caption, “ATIKU IS COMING.” President Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed this in a post on X late Monday, saying Abdullahi had been arraigned before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna. The tweet read, “An avowed supporter of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar now faces trial in Kaduna for circulating a document purportedly written by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to the President of the United States of America. “The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi (aka Sardaunan Samari), was arrested on 28 September for sharing the fake document on his Facebook page with the caption “ATIKU IS COMING.” “Mubarak admitted to investigators that he shared the fake document and apologised for his actions. The contrition was not enough. “The DSS arraigned him before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna, which ordered his remand at the Nigerian Correctional Centre, Kaduna,” adding that the agency “has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against him at the Federal High Court, Kaduna.” Onanuga, however, said the DSS would continue to demonstrate its ability to identify people involved in circulating what he described as misleading information online. Meanwhile, human rights activist and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) Omoyele Sowore criticised the arrest, accusing the DSS of being used to suppress dissent. In a post on X on Tuesday, Sowore questioned the agency’s involvement in the case and described the arrest as an attempt to silence a citizen over an online post. “How low will you go, #OfficialAPCNg and the #officialABAT regime? How on earth do you reduce a national security agency like the #OfficialDSSNG to a mere vacuum cleaner, deployed to sweep up dissenting voices in your inordinate ambition to subdue every citizen simply because you are afraid to face the Nigerian people and account for your disastrous reign?” he wrote. Sowore added, “Arresting a hapless citizen for posting a document online – sad! Shame on all of you! A day of reckoning is coming, when you too will be held accountable for your actions. That day is coming sooner than you think. Very soon!” Neither Atiku nor his media aide, Phrank Shaibu, had publicly reacted to the development as of the time of writing. item.title: EKO HOTELS AT 50: THE NIGHT AFRICAN HOSPITALITY STOPPED ASKING FOR A SEAT AT THE GLOBAL TABLE
item.description: The Legacy Gala & Awards night: Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. In LAGOS, NIGERIA, 2nd of OCTOBER 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history. Others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre. Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party. It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow. Fifty years of memories finding their voices. Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa. And for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A HOTEL BECAME PART OF A NATION’S STORY There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory. Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalised. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world. For others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation. It must become an experience. A cultural encounter. An economic opportunity. A reason to travel. A reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. THAT NIGHT, AFRICA WORE HER CROWN The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society. item.title: Elevate Africa 2026 Convening: Press Conference Sets Stage for Accra Gathering Under “Africa: Defining Her Future”
item.description: The countdown to one of Africa’s most anticipated leadership gatherings is officially underway. On Monday, October 26, 2026, Elevate Africa held a curtain-raiser press conference in Accra, Ghana, setting the stage for its 2026 Annual Convening. Held under the powerful theme “Africa: Defining Her Future,” the main convening will take place on October 28–29, 2026, at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra, bringing together heads of state, traditional rulers, policymakers, creatives, investors, and diaspora leaders. DAY ONE: THE PRESS CONFERENCE The press conference served as a powerful preview of the conversations to come, with four key voices setting the tone for the days ahead: 1. Her Majesty Olori Atuwatse III — Queen Consort of the Warri Kingdom and Co-Founder of Elevate Africa The Queen Consort delivered a stirring call for African-led solutions, declaring: “Time has come for Africa to take up the pen and write its own future.” She emphasized that meaningful transformation requires collaboration across governments, business, and civil society, stating: “Solutions can only be truly driven by those who are leading nations, leading companies, leading in different sectors.” She also highlighted the Elevate Africa Fellowship, which empowers mid-career professionals to reshape the continent’s narrative from one of problems to one of solutions. 2. Kofi Okyere Darko (KOD) — Director of Diaspora Affairs, Office of the President of Ghana Representing the Ghanaian government, KOD underscored the indispensable role of the global African diaspora. “We can’t elevate Africa to the next level without the participation of the diaspora,” he stated, noting that Africans abroad possess valuable knowledge, skills, networks, and resources that can drive economic transformation. He also highlighted Ghana’s commitment to deepening diaspora engagement beyond tourism, encouraging investment and entrepreneurship. 3. Emmanuel Ikubese — Elevate Africa Fellow (2026 Cohort) Bringing the perspective of emerging leaders, Ikubese advocated for pan-African collaboration among professionals. He argued that the continent’s development relies on collective intelligence and the mobilization of its vast talent pool. 4. Dr. Rex Idaminabo — Chief Partnership Officer, Elevate Africa Closing the session, Dr. Idaminabo framed the convening as a decisive moment for the continent. “Africa’s transformation is a decision, and for that to happen, we want everyone to take part,” he said, emphasizing that the fellowship has united participants from 23 African countries to build resilience and support one another. OTHER KEY VOICES AT THE PRESS CONFERENCE INCLUDE: Prince Moses — Director of Strategy, Africa Prosperity Network (APN) He spoke on economic integration, urging the removal of barriers to the movement of people, capital, and goods across the continent, and highlighted the gap between Africa’s 1.5 billion-person market and its low intra-African trade volume. item.title: Gunmen kill seven in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen on Monday night stormed Georo community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing seven persons in an attack that threw residents into panic. The attackers, who invaded the community at about 10:20pm, reportedly opened fire sporadically, killing some persons in their shops and others at a local restaurant. A member of the community, Mr Bot Silas, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen stormed the community at about 10:20pm and started shooting sporadically.” Silas said, “Some of the victims were killed in their shops, while others were attacked at a local restaurant where food was being prepared.” He added, “Seven persons were killed in the attack, and the incident caused serious panic among residents of the community.” Silas said, “The attackers came at night and started shooting, forcing residents to scamper for safety.” Reacting to the incident, spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attack and described it as unacceptable. Tengwong said, “The killing of innocent people in Georo is condemnable and must not be allowed to continue.” “I call on the relevant security agencies to intensify efforts to protect communities and apprehend those responsible for the attack.” Tengwong added, “We call on the relevant security agencies to investigate the incident, bring the perpetrators to justice and ensure that residents can live and carry out their legitimate activities without fear.” The post Gunmen kill seven in Plateau community appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US midterms: Five issues shaping the vote
item.description: Americans voting in the November 3 midterm elections will decide who controls Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency, along with dozens of governorships and thousands of state offices. The campaign is playing out against an unusually combustible mix of economic anxiety, war, immigration battles, corruption concerns and unease over rapidly expanding artificial intelligence. Polls asking voters about priorities use different methodologies, but they broadly agree on the dominance of pocketbook concerns. An October Pew survey found economic issues easily topped voters’ worries, while a September Emerson poll put the Iran war, jobs, tariffs, gas prices, immigration and AI regulation among the most important factors in voting decisions. Here are five issues shaping the midterms: – It’s the economy – Affordability remains issue number one. Inflation was running at 3.7 percent in September, but the political problem goes beyond the headline rate, with voters paying more for gasoline, housing, electricity, groceries and borrowing. Pew found that 65 percent of Americans see Trump’s economic policies as hurtful to the economy. Another survey, from the Joseph Rainey Center for Public Policy, found 57 percent placing groceries, gas or utilities among their top three issues. Trump’s tariffs feed directly into the debate, with opponents blaming them for higher costs while the administration argues they protect American industry and raise revenue. – Iran war – A foreign war has become a domestic pocketbook issue. The conflict with Iran, underway since February, has driven energy costs higher and become deeply unpopular. Emerson’s September survey rated the Iran war the single most important issue among those it tested, while Reuters/Ipsos found only 34 percent approving of Trump’s handling of the conflict. Republican candidates in several competitive races have called for the fighting to end, and four Republican senators joined Democrats in a September vote seeking to rein it in. – Immigration – The strength of Trump’s signature political talking point has become more complicated. The president returned to office promising mass deportations, but support has eroded following controversy over deaths during arrests and detention, and aggressive ICE operations. Reuters/Ipsos found 55 percent disapproved of Trump’s handling of immigration. Marist, meanwhile, found Democrats and Republicans essentially level on which party voters trusted more on the issue — a striking change from the clear Republican advantage of 2024. The shift is particularly notable among Latinos. A survey across competitive House districts found 62 percent of Latino voters disapproved of the administration’s deportation and immigration enforcement. – Trump, money and power – The president himself is an issue — including how he uses the office. item.title: We’re not responsible for hunger in Nigeria – PDP fires back at APC
item.description: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) on Monday says it is not responsible for hunger in Nigeria, advising the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to stop the blame game. The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed said this in a statement on Monday in Abuja. According to Mohammed, the PDP’s attention has been drawn to the statement made by the APC Publicity Secretary, Felix Moka, during his appearance on a show on Monday. ”In statement, he blamed the PDP for the hunger and economic hardship currently confronting Nigerians. “The PDP also notes similar remarks reportedly made by President Bola Tinubu in Kaduna during the flag-off of his 2027 re-election campaign. “The PDP considers these statements as attempts to evade responsibility and divert public attention from the pressing challenges facing the country under the APC-led administration. “Our message to the APC is simple: stop the blame game and start taking responsibility. Nigerians deserve solutions, not excuses. “The government in power must address the country’s challenges through concrete, measurable, and sustainable actions that will bring meaningful relief to citizens. “The PDP is not responsible for the hunger Nigerians are experiencing today. The APC must own its record, address the nation’s challenges, and deliver on its promises to Nigerians.” He added that the government in power must answer for its stewardship and present a credible path towards economic recovery, food security, and a better standard of living for all Nigerians. Mohammed said that rather than engaging in political blame games, the APC should explain what it intended to do to make food affordable, support farmers, and strengthen local food production. He also advised the ruling party to tell Nigerians how it intended to create jobs, improve security, fight corruption, improve electricity supply, reduce transportation costs, and restore the purchasing power of ordinary Nigerians, among other pressing concerns. The PDP national publicity secretary further said that while the party acknowledged some of the achievements recorded by President Tinubu’s administration, where applicable, it rejected any attempt to use its 16 years in government as a blanket justification for the shortcomings of the present administration. “Acknowledging any genuine achievements must not be misconstrued as an endorsement of all government policies or an acceptance of attempts to shift responsibility for current economic difficulties to previous PDP-led administrations. “After more than 10 years of APC in office, Nigerians deserve answers, not excuses. “The APC must tell Nigerians what it has achieved, outline the concrete measures it is taking to address the country’s present-day challenges, and demonstrate its commitment to improving the welfare of citizens rather than continually dragging the PDP into its own shortcomings,” he said. item.title: FG’s reforms rewrite Nigeria’s economic underperformance story – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu says his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to unlock the country’s enormous economic potential. Tinubu, represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, stated this on Monday at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit held in Abuja. The president said his administration began its tenure with difficult economic decisions aimed at addressing structural challenges that had hindered Nigeria’s growth and development for decades. “There is no shortcut to economic growth,” stressing that the government had embarked on a difficult economic reset to establish a sustainable foundation for national prosperity. According to him, the administration is pursuing its original mission of transforming Nigeria’s economic fortunes and reversing years of performance below the country’s potential. “We came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long,” Tinubu said. He explained that the reforms were necessary to dismantle longstanding economic barriers, strengthen national productivity and create opportunities for Nigerians across different sectors. The president said rescuing the economy involved more than improving economic indicators, noting that the ultimate objective was to improve livelihoods and expand opportunities for citizens. “For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young jobseekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators,” he said. Tinubu stressed that economic stability remained essential to harnessing the opportunities presented by Nigeria’s growing population and abundant human and natural resources. “We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy,” he said. He said the administration had created conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand their operations and generate productive employment. According to him, the government has introduced reforms to dismantle structural barriers that prevented the country’s resources from translating into widespread prosperity. “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth,” the President said. Tinubu said the administration was encouraged by the progress recorded so far, adding that the next phase required greater attention to productivity, employment quality and the effective utilisation of the workforce. He stressed the need to improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential of Nigeria’s underutilised workforce. The President said sustainable prosperity would require greater productivity from workers, businesses and investments across the economy. “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment,” he said. item.title: Ballon d’Or: Harry Kane’s crowning moment
item.description: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose trophy collection does not do justice to his remarkable talent and consistency. The Bayern Munich striker, 33, is the first Englishman to win football’s most coveted individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane’s numbers are staggering and the England captain appears to be improving with age, with 73 goals for club and country last season. In September he became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, hitting the landmark on his 98th league appearance for Bayern. He is also Tottenham’s all-time leading scorer with 280 goals, England’s record scorer with 91, and the highest-scoring English player in the Champions League (58). But for all his personal achievements in club and international football, Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and was in England teams that twice lost the European Championship final. Kane’s lethal finishing is not the only string to his bow. Honing an instinct he first developed as a youth team player, Kane has also blossomed into a gifted playmaker. “I feel like I’ve always had the passing range and the vision and the football brain — the game understanding — throughout my whole career, and I think that’s just flourished these last couple of years especially, these last few years since I’ve been here at Bayern,” he told UEFA.com. – Ageing like fine wine – The clean-cut Kane, married to his childhood sweetheart Katie Goodland, is an understated throwback in an era of football bling. But it has not always been plain sailing for a player who struggled to make an impression early in his career with Tottenham and was farmed out to other clubs on loan. There were almost two years between Kane’s first Spurs goal, against Shamrock Rovers in 2011, and his next, against Hull in 2013. Even after his breakthrough season in 2014/15, he was dubbed a “one-season wonder”, an accusation that has proved laughably wide of the mark. Bayern boss Vincent Kompany has spoken of Kane’s numerous qualities, including his distribution, work rate and “game intelligence”. “To combine that side of his game with the numbers he has, you have to do the job to help the team progress and then still arrive in the box, so it is not an easy thing,” Kompany said. “That is something we have seen and been able to enjoy, and that was maybe underestimated at the time in England, but he is ageing like fine wine so I am just enjoying seeing that side of his game for us as well.” Bayern teammate Jonathan Tah praised Kane’s remarkable work ethic after seeing it up close. “I played against him a lot and every time he got better — now I’m playing with him I see why,” he told the Times. “He’s never satisfied, you see him working before and after training. item.title: Nigerians need president with competence, capacity, compassion, commitment – Peter Obi
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has described the kind of leader Nigerians need. Read Also: * Full list: NDC unveils 2027 presidential campaign council * 2027: APC dismisses NDC’s allegation of blocking venues, billboards for campaign According to the former Anambra State governor, the administration of President Bola Tinubu lacked “competence, capacity, compassion and commitment required to address the country’s problems,” insisting that Nigerians needed a president who would be available and responsive. He spoke on Monday night in Abuja at the inauguration of the party’s 118-member National Presidential Campaign Council ahead of January 16, 2027, where certificates of return were presented to NDC candidates. Peter Obi called for a new leadership for Nigeria, saying the country is facing serious challenges under the present administration. Obi said: “Everything is collapsing. Nigerians are looking for new leadership, and I can assure you that we will provide it.” Obi, who is contesting the presidency alongside his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, noted that the country needed a fundamental change in leadership, governance philosophy and public resource management, insisting that Nigerians could no longer afford a government that failed to address their most pressing challenges. NEC meeting The events followed an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee, NEC, and the inauguration of the newly acquired national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja, which is expected to serve as the party’s administrative headquarters and presidential campaign coordination centre. The NDC intensified its preparations for the 2027 general elections with the inauguration of its newly acquired national secretariat in Jabi, Abuja, the formal inauguration of its National Presidential Campaign Council and the presentation of certificates of return to candidates elected to contest on the party’s platform. The NDC presidential candidate, who warned against electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the NDC would demand a free, fair and credible election. He urged supporters to go into the country and campaign for the party, just as he warned those who might harass NDC supporters or attempt to manipulate the election that the party would resist such actions. Obi said the party would focus on making Nigeria work and restoring the confidence of Nigerians in their country. Addressing party leaders and supporters at the dinner, Obi painted a grim picture of Nigeria’s socioeconomic conditions, citing poverty, unemployment, insecurity, corruption and the education crisis as evidence of what he described as the failure of the present administration. He argued that the responsibility of government was to solve problems rather than blame political opponents, insisting that an NDC administration would be judged by the improvements it delivered to citizens. item.title: Global initiative support group to inaugurate canvassers, friday in Ughelli
item.description: A formidable political support group, the Global Initiative Support Group for Sheriff 2027, will inaugurate Coordinators and Canvassers across the 25 Local Government Areas of Delta State, on Friday, October 30, at Oharisi Primary School, Ughelli, Delta State. The inauguration ceremony, scheduled for 10am, will be performed by the Delta State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Chief Solomon Arenyeka. Convener of the group, Sir Festus Ahon, its Chairman, Chief Josiah Ntekume, and Secretary, Barr. Abednego Dikame disclosed in a statement issued in Asaba, Monday. The inauguration is expected to formally empower the Coordinators and Canvassers of the group to go into the streets across the state, including rural and riverine communities, to Canvass votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. The choice of Ughelli as the venue places the event within the political landscape of Delta State, where political groups and grassroots mobilisation remain important features of party activities. The presence of Arenyeka, who is expected to inaugurate the group, is also expected to lend political significance to the occasion as members of the group formally begin their activities. The organisers urged members and supporters to take note of the venue and time of the ceremony, expressing their readiness to massively woo voters for candidates of the APC. item.title: 2027: APC dismisses NDC’s allegation of blocking venues, billboards for campaign
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Cynthia Alo & Kafayat Kokumo ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has accused the All Progressives Congress, APC, of frustrating its campaign preparations ahead of the 2027 general elections by allegedly denying it access to event venues and billboards. National Publicity Secretary of the NDC, Osa Director, made the allegation during an interview on ARISE TV yesterday, insisting that the party will not be intimidated or prevented from exercising its democratic rights. He said the party had encountered difficulties securing venues despite making payments, adding that its latest venue was the fourth it had attempted to use for its planned activities. “This is the fourth venue we are paying for. We kept this one under wraps until just a few hours ago when we issued the press release, only for us to be called that the political marauders have come and said they are the owners of the land, so we should take back our money,” he said. He added that the party will proceed with its activities, despite the alleged restrictions, insisting that no individual or political party owned the country. “Nigeria belongs to us all. Nobody owns Nigeria. We fought, we used our life and sweat and blood to fight for this democracy we are enjoying today. So who is that person to tell me that I will not have a right to exercise my freedom of speech and freedom of assembly?” he said. The NDC spokesman also alleged that the party had been denied access to billboards but maintained that such restrictions would not prevent it from reaching voters. Speaking on the party’s campaign preparations, Director dismissed suggestions that the NDC was starting late, saying its presidential candidate had already held several town hall meetings across the country. He said the party had held at least four meetings and had nearly completed its engagements across the zones, arguing that its approach differed from campaigns focused on rallies, music and public displays. The party was scheduled to inaugurate its national campaign council, commission its newly acquired national secretariat in Jabi, Abuja, and present certificates of return to its candidates yesterday, the spokesman said the certificates were part of a formal process, adding that the candidates had already been uploaded to the Independent National Electoral Commission’s portal. He also announced that the party would publicly present a statement of its finances and challenged the APC to do the same, saying Nigerians would be surprised by the figures. He defended the party’s anti-defection oath, adding that it was intended to address political defections and what he described as irresponsible politicking. item.title: NYSC, UNN disowned ex-minister Uche Nnaji’s certificates, ICPC witness tells court
item.description: An investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. The witness, Suprintendent of Police, Yakubu Ibrahim, testified as the first prosecution witness in the trial of Nnaji, who is facing a six-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/389/2026, bordering on alleged corruption, fraud, conferring corrupt advantage and providing false information through the alleged presentation of forged university degree and national service certificates. The investigator, who was led in evidence by the prosecution counsel, J. A. Mumini (SAN), said he was part of the ICPC team that investigated two petitions against the defendant. The witness said his team was assigned to investigate the matter after the commission received two separate petitions alleging certificate forgery against Nnaji. He said the Chairman of the Special Task Force directed an investigation, prompting the commission to request relevant documents from the National Assembly, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), University of Nigeria, Nsukka and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). He told the court that the team wrote to UNN to authenticate the Bachelor of Science certificate in Microbiology/Biochemistry allegedly submitted by Nnaji to the Senate. According to him, the university responded that it did not issue the certificate to the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu for the 2027 election. The witness added that the team also contacted the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) over a discharge certificate 15th May 1986, but the NYSC equally disowned it, maintaining that it did not issue any such certificate to the ex-minister. Ibrahim further told the court that UNN supplied the investigators with the defendant’s academic records, including a notice of withdrawal issued over his failure to obtain the required grade in a course. When shown copies of the correspondence between the ICPC and the two institutions, the witness identified the documents, following which the prosecution sought to tender them in evidence. Defence counsel, Wole Olanipekun (SAN), said he would allow the documents to be admitted at that stage but reserve his objection until later. On the steps taken to interview the defendant, Ibrahim said the head of his section issued an invitation, but investigators could not locate his address. He said a copy of the invitation, dated May 5, 2026, was subsequently sent to the defendant’s email address and WhatsApp number. item.title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
item.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country. 1. Higher temperatures and health risks One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year. The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur. Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers. Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies.
